describe api in 100 words in 100 words.groq: An API, or Application Programming Interface, is a set of rules and protocols that enables different software components to communicate. It defines how requests are formatted, how data is exchanged, and what responses look like, abstracting underlying implementation details. Developers use APIs to access functionality of operating systems, libraries, web services, or hardware without needing to understand internal code. APIs can be local, such as library calls, or remote, like RESTful web services using HTTP. By providing a consistent contract, APIs promote modularity, reuse, and integration, allowing diverse applications to interoperate efficiently. They also enable rapid development and scalable architectures.
